- Overestimate prices when sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, especially if recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33) and recent prices show downward momentum.
- Avoid sharp upward forecasts after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and then correct, so reduce peak forecasts by 5–10% if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) but price history shows mean reversion, reduce forecasted peak by 10–15% to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast, especially after a spike, assume model is overfitting to recent highs — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is high, consider mean reversion — adjust downward by 5–10% unless strong macro support exists.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.2x the 18-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish and price is trending upward.
